description: High-Risk Maternal / Obstetric population. Clinical context: All patients are female ages 18-45. Gestational diabetes (O24.419) is managed with diet/insulin — metformin is second-line. Pre-eclampsia (O14.x) diagnosis requires BP ≥140/90 plus proteinuria. HELLP syndrome is a severe pre-eclampsia variant with hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets. Postpartum hemorrhage (O72.x) requires rapid intervention. All diagnoses use O-code prefix (obstetric complications).
do_not_flag: Blood pressure 140-200/90-130 in pre-eclampsia patients — diagnostic threshold for pre-eclampsia is ≥140/90; this is expected, not implausible
Glucose 140-400 mg/dL in gestational diabetes patients — GDM is defined by glucose intolerance; high glucose is the defining lab finding
Hemoglobin 6.0-9.9 g/dL in postpartum hemorrhage patients — hemorrhage causes acute anemia; Hgb drop is expected
Platelets 50-149 K/uL in pre-eclampsia patients — thrombocytopenia is a feature of HELLP syndrome
ALT/AST 57-300 U/L in pre-eclampsia — liver involvement in HELLP; not a medication side effect in this cohort
Urine protein 21-500 mg/dL in pre-eclampsia — proteinuria is a defining diagnostic criterion
Magnesium sulfate IV in inpatient patients — standard seizure prophylaxis for severe pre-eclampsia during labor/delivery
Insulin use without Type 2 diabetes diagnosis — gestational diabetes (O24.419) requires insulin; O24 code is sufficient, E11 not required
High obstetric visit frequency (14/year) — prenatal guidelines recommend 12-14 visits for high-risk pregnancy

required_drug_classes.rationale: Pre-eclampsia and gestational hypertension affect 55%+ of this cohort; antihypertensives are required treatment.

required_checks: VERIFY that only female patients appear in this cohort. If any male patients have obstetric O-code diagnoses, flag CRITICAL.
VERIFY that glucose tolerance labs appear in the population (GDM is primary diagnosis). If no glucose labs present, flag HIGH.
VERIFY that BP readings of 140+ systolic appear in at least some encounters — pre-eclampsia is a major cohort driver and requires elevated BP.
CHECK that prenatal vitamins or obstetric medications appear in the medication list. If only psychiatric medications, flag MEDIUM.
